chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who performed li'an (cursing) with his wife, so he swore four testimonies by Allah, then abstained (from swearing) in the fifth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he abstained in the fifth, then she is his wife, and he is whipped; and if the woman abstained from that, when the oath is upon her, then upon her is similar to that.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about the cursing, would he curse standing or sitting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The cursing and what resembles it is from standing.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about a man who divorced his wife before he entered (consummated) with her, so she claimed that she was pregnant. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she establishes the proof that he loosened the veil (consummated), then denies the child, he can curse her, then she is irrevocably divorced from him, and upon him is the complete dower.'

key_terms.سِتْرًا: Veil or covering (referring to the marital bed/consummation)
key_terms.لَاعَنَ: Performed li'an (mutual cursing/oath-taking to resolve paternity dispute)
key_terms.نَكَلَ: Abstained or hesitated from swearing the oath

ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences of li'an if the husband or wife abstains from the fifth oath, and how is dower handled in pre-consummation divorce with pregnancy claims?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the procedural mechanics of li'an, emphasizing that the physical posture (standing or sitting) is secondary to the verbal declaration, a nuance highlighted by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It further clarifies the specific application of li'an in cases of pre-consummation divorce where paternity is disputed, linking the dissolution of marriage to the payment of the full dower. These rulings underscore the Shia jurisprudential focus on the precise conditions of the fifth oath and the evidentiary burden in establishing lineage.
